cultural.vision_reason: This is a documentary 19th-century photograph of a Winnebago (Ho-Chunk) chief and community gathered before a tipi with decorative panels, clothing, and other people, matching the claimed ethnicity's daily/ceremonial life.

physical.title: photographic print (black and white); stereoscope photograph
physical.classification: photographic print (black and white); stereoscope photograph
physical.summary:
Photograph (black and white), half of a mounted stereoscope photograph; portrait of Wak-ka-mas, a Winnebago chief, in front of a tipi, speaking to a group of men, women, and children seated on the ground, and two men sitting in a tree in the background; the Winnebago wear cloth headscarf’s, shirts and leggings, with the exception of the man on the right who wears a hat with a feather, and a man lying down who holds a tomahawk; two women and a child sit  on the right, and a baby in a baby-carrier wrapped in cloth situated on the left beside a woman; tipi has square section of embroidered patterned at entrance; United States of America. 
Albumen print
